title: The right opening: あく, あける, ひらく, ひらける
summary: Four words for opening that show how flexible self-move and other-move are: あく / あける for open and shut, ひらく for unfolding.

blocks.text: 開く and 開ける look like two pairs of self-move / other-move verbs, and up to a point they are: **あく** (self-move) and **あける** (other-move). The kanji is the same for ひらく and ひらける, so the writer uses hiragana when she specifically wants ひらく.
Rule of thumb: **あく** is self-move (the door opens by itself) and **あける** is other-move (I open it), the same pair as lesson 15.
ドアが開く: the door does it.
瓶を開ける: I open the bottle.
Japanese speakers sometimes use 開く in an other-move way, as in 目を開く. The advice is to stay safe: **あける** is always right for other-move, whether the object is a door, a mouth or a bottle.
ひらく and ひらける

**ひらく** is about the kind of opening: something that **unfolds or spreads out**, like a flower or a hand. It is both self-move and other-move. **あく / あける** is simply becoming open instead of closed, like a lid. For an umbrella the usual verb is **さす**. **ひらける** is closer to a state: 運がひらける means your luck opens and stays open from then on.

blocks.en: (I) open the shop at nine in the morning. (for the day)

blocks.text: Compare the two shops. 店をあける is opening up for business today. 店をひらく is opening a new shop for the first time.

blocks.jp: 駅の前に新しい店をひらく。
blocks.en: (I) open a new shop in front of the station.
(I) close my hand into a fist, then open it like a flower.

blocks.jp: 目をひらくと、朝だった。
blocks.en: When I opened my eyes, it was morning.
One's luck opens up (and stays that way).

items: **あく / あける**: simply become open or open it (doors, bottles, mouths).
**ひらく**: unfold, spread out (flowers, hands); both self- and other-move.
**ひらける**: a state of being opened out (luck, a view).
If unsure, あける is a safe other-move verb.

questions.note: あく is self-move: the window is the main carriage, が.
questions.en: The window opened in the wind.

questions.note: あける is other-move: it does something to a thing, を.
questions.en: My younger brother opened the box.

questions.instruction: Which verb fits a flower opening out?
questions.note: ひらく is about unfolding and spreading out.

questions.instruction: Which is the safe other-move verb for a door, a mouth or a bottle?
questions.note: あける is always right for other-move.

questions.prompt: 友だちが小さな本屋を＿＿＿。
questions.note: Starting a business is ひらく, an other-move opening.
questions.en: My friend opened a small bookstore.

questions.prompt: ひらける is closer to a state of being opened out.
questions.note: 運がひらける: the opening stays that way.
questions.en: ひらける: to open out.

questions.instruction: What does ひらける suggest?
questions.prompt: 山の上で、広い空がひらけた。
options: A view opens out and stays open
questions.note: ひらける is a state of being opened out, like a view.
questions.en: On the mountain, a wide sky opened out.

questions.note: あける is other-move, and 口を is its object.
questions.en: That child is sleeping with his mouth open.

questions.prompt: It was hot, so I opened the window.
questions.note: An other-move verb with を.
questions.en: It was hot, so I opened the window.

questions.instruction: Which verb is usual for an umbrella?
questions.note: For an umbrella the usual verb is さす.
あく is self-move: the shop opens by itself.
A hand spreading out is ひらく.
questions.en: The baby spread out its hand.

questions.note: あく moves itself; あける moves something else.
ひらく is also other-move: the book takes を.
A flower opens by itself: ひらく, and あける needs an object.

questions.instruction: Which verb suits unfolding or spreading out?
questions.note: ひらく is the unfolding opening.

questions.prompt: The flowers opened in the garden.
questions.note: ひらく as self-move: the flowers are the main carriage.
questions.en: The flowers opened in the garden.

questions.note: あく is self-move: the door is the carriage.

questions.instruction: Which verb says someone's luck opens and stays open?
questions.note: ひらける is closer to a state.
目 is an object, so use the other-move あける.

questions.prompt: ひらく can be both self-move and other-move.
questions.note: ひらく: the flower opens, I open a shop.
